title: 81. Numeracy & Number Systems: Converting Binary and Hexadecimal Integers
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a binary integer to hexadecimal by grouping bits in blocks of four.
questions.question: What is \(1010_2\) in hexadecimal?
questions.explanation: Group from the right into four-bit blocks, padding on the left if needed: \(1010\). Convert each block: \(1010_2\to A_{16}\). This gives \(A_{16}\). The alternative assigns a wrong hexadecimal digit to at least one block.
questions.hint: Group the binary digits into blocks of four from the right and convert one block at a time.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a hexadecimal integer to binary using four-bit digit equivalents.
questions.question: What is \(F_{16}\) in binary?
questions.explanation: Replace each hexadecimal digit by its four-bit binary group: \(F_{16}\to1111_2\). Joining the groups gives \(1111_2\). Removing leading zeros gives \(1111_2\). The alternative changes a bit and therefore represents a different value.
questions.hint: Replace each hexadecimal digit by four binary bits, then join the groups in order.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a binary integer to hexadecimal by grouping bits in blocks of four.

questions.explanation: Group from the right into four-bit blocks, padding on the left if needed: \(1101\). Convert each block: \(1101_2\to D_{16}\). This gives \(D_{16}\). The alternative assigns a wrong hexadecimal digit to at least one block.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a hexadecimal integer to binary using four-bit digit equivalents.
questions.question: What is \(1A_{16}\) in binary?
questions.explanation: Replace each hexadecimal digit by its four-bit binary group: \(1_{16}\to0001_2\), \(A_{16}\to1010_2\). Joining the groups gives \(00011010_2\). Removing leading zeros gives \(11010_2\). The alternative swaps the last two bits and therefore represents \(25\) instead of \(26\).
questions.hint: Replace each hexadecimal digit by four binary bits, then join the groups in order.

questions.hint: Group the binary digits into blocks of four from the right and convert one block at a time.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a binary integer to hexadecimal by grouping bits in blocks of four.
questions.question: What is \(10101010_2\) in hexadecimal?
questions.explanation: Group from the right into four-bit blocks, padding on the left if needed: \(1010\ 1010\). Convert each block: \(1010_2\to A_{16}\), \(1010_2\to A_{16}\). This gives \(AA_{16}\). The alternative assigns a wrong hexadecimal digit to at least one block.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a hexadecimal integer to binary using four-bit digit equivalents.
questions.question: What is \(B7_{16}\) in binary?
questions.explanation: Replace each hexadecimal digit by its four-bit binary group: \(B_{16}\to1011_2\), \(7_{16}\to0111_2\). Joining the groups gives \(10110111_2\), which has no leading zeros to remove. The alternative writes the second block as \(1011_2\) instead of \(0111_2\) and therefore represents \(BB_{16}\), not \(B7_{16}\).
questions.hint: Replace each hexadecimal digit by four binary bits, then join the groups in order.
